speaker: Unknown
en: Today I'm going to be talking about the state of the art of physical intelligence.
zh: 今天我将要谈论物理智能的最前沿技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in particular, two years ago, I founded a company called Physical Intelligence.
zh: 特别是，两年前，我创办了一家名为 Physical Intelligence 的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're really interested in how we can basically develop any robot or allow any robot to do any task in the real world.
zh: 我们真的很感兴趣我们如何基本上开发任何机器人或允许任何机器人在现实世界中做任何任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I actually spoke at this event a year ago last year.
zh: 其实我去年在这个活动上讲过话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at the event last year, I shared some of our progress at the company, at Physical Intelligence, where we could do things, really complicated tasks, like unloading and folding laundry.
zh: 在去年的活动中，我分享了我们公司在 Physical Intelligence 的一些进展，在那我们可以做事情，真正复杂的任务，像卸货和折叠衣物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I also talked about how, for the first time, we showed how robots can do useful tasks in environments and rooms they've never been in before.
zh: 我也谈到了，我们第一次展示了机器人如何在它们以前从未去过的环境和房间中做有用的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, since then, since one year ago, we have gotten robots to do a lot of other really cool things.
zh: 现在，从那时起，从一年前开始，我们已经让机器人做了许多其他真的很酷的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, we've gotten robots to be able to wash a greasy pan in the top right, or peel a carrot in the video below that, or make a grilled cheese sandwich in the video below that, or slice a zucchini, and so forth.
zh: 所以例如，我们已经让机器人能够洗一个油腻的平底锅，在右上角那个视频里，或者刮胡萝卜在下面的视频里，或者在再下面的视频里做烤芝士三明治，或者切片西葫芦，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what I'd really like to focus on today isn't cool videos of robots doing lots of different things, but what it actually takes to get robots to be useful in the real world.
zh: 但我今天真正想关注的不是机器人做各种各样很酷的视频，而是让机器人在现实世界中有用到底需要什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And specifically, how can we develop general purpose robots that are useful in the real world?
zh: 具体来说，我们如何开发在现实世界中有用的通用机器人？

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, there are two aspects of this.
zh: 现在，这有两个方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is...
zh: 首先是……

speaker: Unknown
en: General purpose, how we can develop general purpose models.
zh: 通用，我们如何开发通用模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the second is actually bringing those models to the real world so that they can actually have an impact and be useful to people.
zh: 第二个实际上是把这些模型带到现实世界，以便它们真正产生影响并造福人类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the first part, I'll talk about being useful in the real world.
zh: 在第一部分，我将谈论在现实世界中有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So to actually bring a technology to the real world, I think we need to figure out, it's helpful to actually look at what people have done in the past to bring AI into the real world.
zh: 所以要把一项技术真正带到现实世界，我认为我们需要弄明白，看看过去人们是如何把 AI 带入现实世界的，这是很有帮助的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we look at a timeline of major production launches that are leveraging technology like machine learning, we can see a timeline like this.
zh: 如果我们看看利用像机器学习这样技术的主要产品发布的时间线，我们可以看到像这样的时间线。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think really the first early examples of machine learning being used in the real world were for things like product recommendations and ad ranking.
zh: 所以我认为真正机器学习在现实世界早期使用的例子是为了像产品推荐和广告排名这样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then five years later we started to see not just machine learning being used but deep learning being used for the same sorts of applications.
zh: 然后五年后，我们开始看到不仅机器学习被使用，而且深度学习被用于同样的应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this was a really exciting advance because deep learning is an algorithm that actually isn't like you can kind of really apply it out of the box to scenarios that involve really complex like inputs and outputs and so forth and it makes it easier to translate to other applications.
zh: 这是一个非常令人兴奋的进步，因为深度学习是一种算法，实际上它不像你可以真正开箱即用地把它应用于涉及像真正的复杂输入和输出等等的场景，这使得它更容易转化为其他应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: But from there, I think that even more exciting moment in time that we saw in terms of machine learning and AI in production was in 2022 with the launch of ChatGPT.
zh: 但从那里开始，我认为就生产和部署中的机器学习和 AI 而言，我们看到的一个更激动人心的时刻是在 2022 年随着 ChatGPT 的发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this was the first time where we saw a general purpose model truly being used by many different people in the real world.
zh: 这是我们第一次看到通用模型真正被现实世界中许多不同的用户使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Within five days, ChatGPT had reached a million users.
zh: 在五天内，ChatGPT 达到了一百万用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then of course more recently we've seen things like Claude Code also be incredibly useful hopefully to many of us in the real world and other coding agents.
zh: 然后当然最近我们看到像 Claude Code 这样的东西也真的非常有用，希望对现实世界中的我们中的许多人和其他编码智能体也是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now if we look at how AI has been used in the real world and kind of look at this, I think there's a few different takeaways we could make.
zh: 现在如果我们看看 AI 是如何在现实世界中被使用的，大概看看这个，我认为我们可以得出几个不同的结论。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is that
zh: 首先是

speaker: Unknown
en: Generalist models are increasingly being used for real-world problems.
zh: 通用模型正越来越多地用于现实世界的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're actually seeing generalist AI models that can do many, many different things actually be used in the real world.
zh: 所以我们实际上看到可以做许多许多不同事情的通用 AI 模型在现实世界中被使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we see that transition from the left to the right.
zh: 而且我们看到从左边到右边的这种转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I also think that there's a more nuanced observation that we can make from looking at these applications.
zh: 但我也认为，通过观察这些应用程序，我们可以得出一个更微妙的观察。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in particular, if we look at all of these different applications that are used, where machine learning has actually been useful in the real world and actually been profitable and so forth, in all of these applications, the customer is making a decision based off of the recommendation of the AI model, more or less.
zh: 特别是，如果我们看看所有这些被使用的不同应用程序，机器学习实际上在现实世界中有用并且有利可图等等，在所有这些应用程序中，客户或多或少是根据 AI 模型的推荐来做决定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this means that...
zh: 这意味着……

speaker: Unknown
en: If the customer is ultimately like kind of making the decision, this means that if the system makes a mistake, that's okay because usually the person can kind of recognize that or decide what to do even despite that mistake.
zh: 如果客户最终像是做决定的那种人，这意味着如果系统犯了错误，那没关系，因为通常人们可以意识到那一点或决定做什么，尽管有那个错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: So even when these sorts of systems aren't perfect, they're still incredibly useful to different people and there's less pressure on them to be completely perfect.
zh: 所以即使当这类系统不完美时，它们对不同的人仍然非常有用，而且对它们要完全完美的压力较小。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that actually physical AI and robotics is pretty different from this, where if we think about physical AI that are actually operating in the physical world, they have to be directly making decisions that affect the physical world.
zh: 而且我认为实际上物理 AI 和机器人技术与这一点非常不同，在那里如果我们考虑实际上在物理世界中运行的物理 AI，它们必须直接做出影响物理世界的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this means that they're going to be far more useful when they're operating fully autonomously.
zh: 这意味着当它们完全自主运行时，它们会更有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a result, this requires us to develop physical AI systems that make far fewer mistakes than the machine learning systems that have been deployed thus far.
zh: 结果，这要求我们开发物理 AI 系统，它们犯的错误比迄今为止部署的机器学习系统少得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, one really exciting thing to kind of highlight that has happened recently is a year ago Waymo passed the quarter of a million weekly autonomous rides, suggesting that it is really possible to develop a machine learning based system that can operate in a trustworthy and autonomous way directly in the physical world.
zh: 现在，一件真正令人兴奋的事情来强调最近发生的事情是一年前 Waymo 经过了每周二十五万次自主行程，这表明确实有可能开发一种基于机器学习的系统，可以直接以值得信赖的和自主的方式在物理世界中运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that brings a lot of hope and optimism for actually doing the same with the rest of AI in the physical world.
zh: 我认为这给在物理世界的其余部分真正做同样的事情带来了很多希望和乐观。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if we want to develop general purpose robots in the real world, I think we need to think about how we're going to make them autonomous for long periods of time so that they're actually useful rather than something where a human is basing decisions on the predictions of the model.
zh: 所以如果我们想在现实世界开发通用机器人，我认为我们需要思考如何让它们长时间自主，以便它们真正有用，而不是那种人类基于模型的预测做决定的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So to think about long-term autonomy, I want to ground this in a specific example and say that we wanted a robot to make espresso.
zh: 所以为了思考长期自主，我想把它建立在一个具体的例子中，并说我们要一个机器人来做浓缩咖啡。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we want it to actually be useful for us, we need it to make espresso reliably so that we don't have to babysit the robot very frequently in order for it to help serve drinks.
zh: 如果我们希望它真的对我们有用，我们需要它可靠地做浓缩咖啡，这样我们就不用经常盯着机器人以帮助它提供饮料。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even on its own, this task is really difficult.
zh: 即使它自己，这项任务也是非常困难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So actually operating the portafilter requires very precise and forceful control to insert it appropriately.
zh: 所以实际上操作无底把手需要非常精确和有力的控制来适当地插入它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also needs to smoothly handle cups with liquid in it and not spill those cups.
zh: 它还需要平稳地处理装有液体的杯子而不洒出那些杯子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it also needs to have an accurate sense of timing, which often isn't actually an issue in other areas of machine learning.
zh: 它还需要有准确的时机感，这通常在机器学习的其他领域实际上不是问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And not only do we want to do this pretty challenging task, we want to do it with over 90% reliability.
zh: 而且不仅我们想完成这个相当具有挑战性的任务，我们要以超过 90% 的可靠性来完成它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how can we do this?
zh: 那么我们要怎么做呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first step in machine learning is always to collect some data set, train a model, and evaluate how good your model is.
zh: 所以机器学习的第一步总是收集一些数据集，训练一个模型，并评估你的模型有多好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And unfortunately, this rarely works reliably on the very first try.
zh: 遗憾的是，这在第一次尝试时很少能可靠地工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, in practice, then, it's a bit better to then iterate on the model that you've developed, where you will try to collect more data, or improve the quality of the labels in your dataset, or make the labels more detailed, collect more data of the edge cases, the scenarios where it's not working well, adjust the balancing of the dataset, and so forth.
zh: 那么，在实践中，最好是对你开发的模型进行迭代，在此过程中你会尝试收集更多数据，或者提高数据集中标签的质量，或者让标签更详细，收集更多边缘情况的数据，即那些表现不佳的场景，调整数据集的平衡，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And while this generally improves the reliability of the model, people eventually get tired, and it's hard to get really, really high reliability with a person that's manually tuning this.
zh: 虽然这通常能提高模型的可靠性，但人们最终会感到厌倦，而且通过人工微调很难获得非常非常高的可靠性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what would be even better is if the AI system itself can iterate on the scenario in which you want it to have high reliability, where it on its own automatically seeks out places where it needs more data, where it needs more supervision.
zh: 因此，更好的办法是 AI 系统本身可以在你希望其具有高可靠性的场景上进行迭代，让它自动独立地寻找需要更多数据的地方，以及需要更多监督的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we can do this for many, many more iterations because it's automatic rather than a person doing it, then this might be the way to get really, really high, like 99 plus percent reliability from physical AI systems.
zh: 如果我们能进行非常非常多次这样的迭代，因为它是自动的而不是人工做的，那么这可能是让物理 AI 系统获得真正非常高的，比如 99% 以上可靠性的途径。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is the approach that we'll take.
zh: 所以这就是我们要采用的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this looks a lot like a reinforcement learning algorithm that's trying to attempt the task, learn from its failures, and get better and better on its own.
zh: 这看起来很像一种强化学习算法，试图尝试任务，从失败中学习，并自行变得越来越好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then how do we develop a scalable reinforcement learning recipe for robotics?
zh: 那么，我们要如何为机器人开发可扩展的强化学习方案呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, in language models, we have algorithms like PPO and GRPO.
zh: 嗯，在语言模型中，我们有像 PPO 和 GRPO 这样的算法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these have scaled to large language models and have enabled really complex reasoning.
zh: 这些算法已经扩展到大语言模型，并实现了真正复杂的推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's a bit of a challenge in applying this to robotics.
zh: 但将其应用于机器人技术有一点挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is that these algorithms have been trained with millions of attempts, or sometimes even tens of millions of attempts, by scaling up the compute.
zh: 也就是说，这些算法已经通过扩展算力，在数百万次尝试中进行了训练，有时甚至高达数千万次尝试。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because each attempt is simply running the language model in a data center just by using compute.
zh: 因为每次尝试只是在数据中心运行语言模型，只需使用算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we were to translate this very, very approximately to robotics, say we had maybe not millions or tens of millions, but just one million trajectories of a one-minute robot task.
zh: 如果我们将其非常粗略地转换到机器人技术领域，假设我们可能没有数百万或数千万次尝试，而是一百万个一分钟机器人任务的轨迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is even shorter than the Espresso task that I talked about.
zh: 这甚至比我之前提到的 Espresso 任务还要短。

speaker: Unknown
en: This would correspond to 700 robot days to get high reliability for that task.
zh: 这将对应于 700 个机器人天数来获得该任务的高可靠性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, maybe this isn't completely out of the question, but this would be quite challenging to do.
zh: 现在，也许这并非完全不可能，但这做起来会相当具有挑战性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's because the calculus is a little bit different.
zh: 这是因为计算方式有点不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not just running compute to optimize for a use case.
zh: 我们不只是运行算力来针对用例进行优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're actually running the robot in the real world and using the hardware and attempting the task in the real world.
zh: 我们实际上是在现实世界中运行机器人，使用硬件，并在现实世界中尝试任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we'd like to have an algorithm that can iterate much more efficiently.
zh: 因此，我们需要一种能够更高效地进行迭代的算法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are actually ways that we can make these algorithms a lot more efficient.
zh: 实际上有一些方法可以让这些算法效率高得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a couple inefficiencies, like large inefficiencies in these reinforcement learning algorithms for language models.
zh: 所以在这些用于语言模型的强化学习算法中存在一些低效之处，比如很大的低效性。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is that they spend a lot of time on dead end trajectories.
zh: 首先是它们在死胡同轨迹上花费了大量时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe this is okay if you're just spending compute on it, but this would cost a lot in the physical world.
zh: 如果你只是为此花费算力，这也许还可以，但在现实世界中这会代价高昂。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we can look at a concrete example.
zh: 所以我们可以看一个具体的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Say that we want our robot to construct cardboard boxes and stack them on the right.
zh: 假设我们要让机器人制作纸箱并将它们堆叠在右边。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in this trajectory right here, the robot accidentally grabbed two boxes that are flush against each other.
zh: 在这条轨迹中，机器人意外地抓住了两个紧贴在一起的箱子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we let it continue, it would just continue to try to fold that box rather than separate out the two boxes.
zh: 如果我们让它继续下去，它只会继续尝试折叠那个箱子，而不是把这两个箱子分开。

speaker: Unknown
en: And trying to fold two boxes together isn't useful data that will teach the model how to get better at the task.
zh: 试图一起折叠两个箱子并不是有用的数据，不会教导模型如何更好地完成任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that would be kind of wasting a lot of time on the robot attempting to go down the wrong path for solving the problem.
zh: 所以这会在机器人试图沿着解决问题的错误路径走下去时浪费大量时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so instead of spending a lot of time trying to do that task, what we'll do is we'll actually have a human intervene and show the robot what to do and how to recover from that situation.
zh: 因此，与其花大量时间尝试做那个任务，我们要做的是实际上让人类干预并向机器人展示该做什么以及如何从那种情况中恢复。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what you can see here is a human is teleoperating and intervening with the robot and showing it that to recover from this situation, it needs to essentially try to separate out the two boxes.
zh: 所以在这里你可以看到一个人正在远程操作并干预机器人，向它展示为了从这种情况中恢复，它本质上需要尝试将两个箱子分开。

speaker: Unknown
en: It then kind of puts its gripper in, sees if the robot could autonomously recover.
zh: 然后它将夹爪放入，看看机器人是否能自主恢复。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't autonomously recover.
zh: 它没有自主恢复。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the person then intervenes again to help it get back on the right track so that we're efficiently using the data on the robot.
zh: 所以人再次干预以帮助它回到正轨，以便我们高效地使用机器人上的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so this is the first thing that we can do, which is we can show the robot how to recover early, or how to recover so that we're not spending time on dead end trajectories, or at the very least just terminate the episode early.
zh: 好的，所以这是我们可以做的第一件事，就是我们可以尽早向机器人展示如何恢复，或者如何恢复，这样我们就不会在死胡同轨迹上花费时间，或者至少尽早终止这一回合。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the second thing that we can do is PPO and GRPO and these kinds of algorithms, they make many attempts at a single prompt.
zh: 现在，我们可以做的第二件事是，PPO 和 GRPO 以及这类算法，它们对单个提示词进行多次尝试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And depending on the algorithm, they're essentially trying to estimate for these different responses, what is a good response and what's a bad response.
zh: 根据算法的不同，它们本质上是在试图针对这些不同的回复，评估什么是好的回复，什么是坏的回复。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so even for an individual prompt, they're actually going to kind of roll out like 10 or 50 times for that individual prompt.
zh: 所以即使对于单个提示词，它们实际上也会针对那个单独的提示词像推出 10 次或 50 次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're doing this because they're trying to estimate the value of these different attempts to then kind of increase the likelihood of good things and decrease the likelihood of bad things.
zh: 它们这样做是因为它们试图评估这些不同尝试的价值，然后以此增加好事的可能性并减少坏事的可能性。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we can actually amortize this cost.
zh: 但我们实际上可以分摊这种成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rather than trying to collect a lot of attempts for a single prompt, we can amortize this across different prompts and learn a much more general value estimate of what's good and what's bad and use this to improve with our autonomous experience.
zh: 与其试图为单个提示词收集大量尝试，我们可以将其分摊到不同的提示词中，并学习一个更通用的关于好坏的评估，并用它来结合我们的自主经验进行改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what this looks like is we can train a general purpose value function on lots of kind of videos of the robot experience.
zh: 所以这看起来像是，我们可以在大量的机器人经验视频上训练一个通用的价值函数。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this can learn things like if it accidentally unfolds a shirt when it's trying to fold, that that's bad and that's making negative progress.
zh: 这可以学习诸如，如果它在试图折叠时意外地展开了衬衫，那是坏事，那是负面进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's shown in red.
zh: 这用红色显示。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or if it's making kind of forward progress, it recognizes that as well.
zh: 或者如果它正在取得某种正向进展，它也能识别出这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the same value function can also estimate what's good and bad for a completely different scenario, in this case for retrieving an item from a fridge.
zh: 同样的价值函数也可以评估对于完全不同的场景什么是好什么是坏，在这种情况下是从冰箱中取出物品。

zh: 还是说具身数据和硬件的成本会将最好的模型集中在少数资源充足的实验室中？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think this is a good question.
zh: 所以我认为这是一个好问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I do think the cost of embodied data and hardware could very much make this look different, because I think that it's harder to get data, even to distill a model, for example, just readily on the internet.
zh: 所以我确实认为具身数据和硬件的成本会让情况看起来很不同，因为我认为获取数据更难，例如要在互联网上直接蒸馏一个模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think that we've seen pretty large data sets get open sourced as well, and pretty powerful models get open sourced.
zh: 我也认为我们已经看到相当大的数据集被开源，以及相当强大的模型被开源。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's really hard to say exactly what will happen.
zh: 我认为很难确切地说会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, yeah, I don't know.
zh: 所以，是的，我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: The one thing that I will say is that with language models, even aside from democratization like Kimmy and really getting models that perform at the state of the art, even then companies that are focusing a lot on closed source models are also doing a lot of open sourcing.
zh: 我能说的是，对于语言模型，除了像 Kimmy 这样的大众化以及真正获得达到最先进性能的模型之外，即使那样，那些专注于闭源模型的公司也在做很多开源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there are like Gemma, for example, and...
zh: 所以比如说有 Gemma，以及……

speaker: Unknown
en: The GPT open source and so forth.
zh: GPT 开源等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think these companies like to support open source because it actually helps build the ecosystem around the things that they're building.
zh: 我认为这些公司喜欢支持开源，因为它实际上有助于围绕他们正在构建的东西建立生态系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I imagine they're being, I guess I'm optimistic that there will be a strong open source community regardless.
zh: 所以我想他们正在……，我想我很乐观，无论如何都会有一个强大的开源社区。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I don't know if it will exactly play out exactly the way that language models played out.
zh: 但我不确定它是否会完全像语言模型那样发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, the next question is, does the model output raw motor commands directly or does it output a target hand position and let a controller solve for the joint angles and what makes that the right level to learn at?
zh: 好的，下一个问题是，模型是直接输出原始电机命令，还是输出目标手部位置并让控制器求解关节角度，是什么使得那是学习的正确层级？

speaker: Unknown
en: So all the models that I showed were outputting target joint positions.
zh: 所以我展示的所有模型都在输出目标关节位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like, what is the angle of this joint?
zh: 比如，这个关节的角度是多少？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the angle of this joint and so forth that you want to hit?
zh: 这个关节的角度是多少，以此类推，是你想要达到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's a controller, like a PD controller that is trying to then hit that target position for those joints.
zh: 然后有一个控制器，比如一个 PD 控制器，试图为这些关节达到那个目标位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: The model actually is also trained to predict target gripper positions, like where in 3D space should my gripper be.
zh: 该模型实际上还被训练来预测目标夹爪位置，比如我的夹爪在 3D 空间中应该在哪里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you could also use that as well and back out the joint positions.
zh: 你也可以使用它并反推关节位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another thing you could do is you could go directly to motor torques or to voltages or efforts.
zh: 你可以做的另一件事是你可以直接使用电机扭矩或电压或力。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are pros and cons of different options.
zh: 不同的选项各有利弊。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have found controlling joints and controlling in the 3D space of the gripper to both work well.
zh: 我们发现控制关节和控制夹爪的 3D 空间都运作良好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so yeah, there's pros and cons.
zh: 所以是的，各有利弊。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the one thing that would be nice about going directly to the voltages is that you could also get a more stiff
zh: 我认为直接使用电压的一个好处是，你也可以获得一种更硬的

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of output or a less stiff output.
zh: 输出或者一种不那么硬的输出。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas the controller, if you have a fixed controller, then you're not letting your model control that aspect.
zh: 而对于控制器，如果你有一个固定的控制器，那么你就没有让你的模型控制那个方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, yeah, there's different pros and cons.
zh: 所以，是的，有不同的优缺点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think that what we're working seems to work.
zh: 是的，我认为我们正在做的事情似乎有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't seem to be a bottleneck.
zh: 它似乎不是一个瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I often like to focus on the things that seem to be bottlenecks versus things that don't seem to be bottlenecks.
zh: 我经常喜欢关注那些似乎是瓶颈的事情，而不是那些似乎不是瓶颈的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, next question is, do robots need something like imagination, the ability to picture what should happen next before they can become truly useful?
zh: 好的，下一个问题是，机器人是否需要像「想象力」这样的东西，即在它们变得真正有用之前构想下一步应该发生什么的能力？

speaker: Unknown
en: So the PyO7 model that I showed has something like this, where it can kind of imagine what a future image should look like and then try to accomplish that.
zh: 所以我展示的 PyO7 模型有类似的东西，它可以想象未来的图像应该是什么样子，然后尝试实现它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The...
zh: 这个……

speaker: Unknown
en: We found that that leads to improvement.
zh: 我们发现这带来了改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we saw on the short folding example, we saw like a quantitative bump from using that sort of imagination compared to not using it.
zh: 在折叠衬衫的例子中，我们看到与不使用这种想象力相比，使用了这种想象力带来了定量的提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the same time, I think that the model actually performed surprisingly well without that as well.
zh: 同时，我认为该模型在没有那种能力的情况下也表现得惊人地好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were actually hoping, we were thinking about writing an entire paper, an entire technical report just about that capability and that model.
zh: 我们实际上本来希望，正在考虑就写一整篇论文，一整篇关于那种能力和那种模型的技术报告。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the model without that was so good that we felt like we needed to actually have that play a bigger part of the story, because it seemed like that was really delivering in terms of actually getting really strong results.
zh: 但没有那个功能的模型是如此之好，以至于我们觉得我们需要让它发挥更大的作用，因为似乎它真正带来了实际上非常强的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it seems like one design choice.
zh: 所以这似乎是一种设计选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's hard to say if it's going to be a critical component or not.
zh: 很难说它是否会成为一个关键组成部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess the good news with these kinds of models is that if you develop a good data set, you can run experiments and you can continue to test things with the data set that you have quite effectively.
zh: 我想这类模型的好消息是，如果你开发了一个好的数据集，你可以运行实验，你可以继续有效地使用你拥有的数据集来测试东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think that being able to predict the future seems like a very relevant objective compared to predicting future actions.
zh: 我也认为能够预测未来似乎是一个非常相关的目标，相比于预测未来的动作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that should, I would imagine, kind of help in terms of learning from all the data that you have available to you.
zh: 所以这应该，我想，有助于从你拥有的所有数据中学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, yeah, hard to say if LDS should be a critical component or not.
zh: 所以，是的，很难说 LDS 是否应该成为一个关键组成部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like empirically so far it seems to help, although perhaps not as much as you might expect.
zh: 看起来在实证上到目前为止它似乎有帮助，虽然可能没有你预期的那么多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even without that imagination, the robot can do pretty incredible things.
zh: 即使没有那种想象力，机器人也能做一些相当令人难以置信的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, next is right now it seems that robots are doing amazing tasks but in a very slow manner.
zh: 好的，接下来是，现在看来机器人正在做惊人的任务，但是以一种非常缓慢的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is needed to improve the speed?
zh: 需要什么来提高速度？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm really excited about improving the speed.
zh: 我对提高速度真的很兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we did see speed improvements from reinforcement learning.
zh: 而且我们确实看到了来自强化学习（reinforcement learning）的速度提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also have another release called the RL token where we showed actually even faster speed and actually faster speed than human teleop.
zh: 我们还有另一个发布版本叫 RL token，我们在其中展示了实际上更快的速度，而且实际上比人工遥操作（teleop）更快的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think one of the bottlenecks is...
zh: 我认为瓶颈之一是……

speaker: Unknown
en: That when you teleoperate robots to do things, which is the easiest way to teach a robot to do something, people are kind of slow at teleoperating the robot.
zh: 当你遥操作机器人做事情时，这是教机器人做事情最简单的方法，人们在遥操作机器人时有点慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a couple projects in the pipeline that I think have really promising results in terms of getting fast policies.
zh: 我们在管道中有几个项目，我认为在获得快速策略方面有非常有前景的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think more to come there.
zh: 所以我认为那里会有更多的后续进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, I think it's...
zh: 是的，我认为这是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Either you need to figure out how to make the data faster or you need to figure out how to be faster than the data.
zh: 你要么需要弄清楚如何让数据更快，要么需要弄清楚如何比数据更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: We see the evidence of being able to be a little bit faster than the data.
zh: 我们看到了能够比数据更快的证据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in terms of the next steps, it's either to kind of go even further than that or make the data faster.
zh: 就下一步而言，要么是比那走得更远，要么是让数据更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the most surprising task you've seen a robot complete recently?
zh: 你最近看到机器人完成的最令人惊讶的任务是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you want to see it do next?
zh: 你接下来想看到它做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: So the most surprising thing was not really a task, but when we were working on Py07, I personally trained one of the policies for some of the initial tests for assembling this pinwheel.
zh: 所以最令人惊讶的事情实际上不是一个任务，而是当我们致力于 Py07 时，我个人训练了其中一个策略，用于组装这个风车的一些初步测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I was working on training it to construct the pinwheel,
zh: 当我在致力于训练它来构建风车时，

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing that really surprised me was in all the data, we kind of carefully controlled the strategy for how to assemble the pinwheel, where you basically will take the kind of precut piece of paper and take a little pin and insert the pin into a hole in the paper.
zh: 有一件事真的很让我惊讶，那就是在所有数据中，我们小心地控制了组装风车的策略，基本上你会拿那种预切的纸片，拿一个小别针，把别针插入纸上的孔里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in all of the data, we picked up the pin with the right hand and picked up the paper with the left hand and inserted it.
zh: 在所有数据中，我们用右手拿起别针，用左手拿起纸并插入它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the robot kind of started doing that and then it actually made a mistake and the paper ended up on the right side and the pin ended up on the left side.
zh: 机器人开始那样做，然后它实际上犯了个错误，纸到了右边，别针到了左边。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what the robot did is it picked up the paper and it picked up the pin with its left gripper and it put the pin with its left gripper and inserted it into the paper with its right.
zh: 机器人做的是它拿起了纸，用它的左夹爪拿起了别针，用它的左夹爪拿着别针，并将其插入到用右手拿着的纸里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it had never seen data of inserting the pin with its left gripper and...
zh: 它从未见过用左夹爪插入别针的数据，而且……

speaker: Unknown
en: It kind of showed that even that wasn't in the post-training data at all, and it wasn't even in pre-training either, the robot essentially had learned this sort of equivariance between his left hand and his right hand so that it could actually transfer behaviors from one hand to another, despite the fact that that was never in the data.
zh: 这表明甚至那不在后训练数据中，甚至也不在预训练中，机器人本质上已经学习了这种左手和右手之间的等价性，以便它实际上能够将行为从一只手转移到另一只手，尽管那从未在数据中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that was a really cool moment.
zh: 所以那真是一个非常酷的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like I don't know if other people were as excited about it as I was when I shared it with some people, but it kind of shows this kind of emergent capability in these models that I hadn't seen before.
zh: 我觉得我不知道当我与一些人分享时，其他人是否像我一样对它感到兴奋，但它展示了这些模型中我以前从未见过的这种涌现能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, yeah, in terms of what I'd love to see, I don't know.
zh: 然后，是的，就我很想看到的而言，我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love seeing robots do anything.
zh: 我喜欢看机器人做任何事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I guess I think that there's still a long way to push in terms of reliability for robots being able to do tasks for really long periods of time.
zh: 我想我认为在机器人在非常长的时间内能够做任务的可靠性方面，还有很长的路要走。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't necessarily think that much about individual tasks, but more so about capabilities and how to get the next capability from these models.
zh: 我不一定考虑那么多单独的任务，而是更多地考虑能力，以及如何从这些模型中获得下一个能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and so, yeah, anything.
zh: 是的，所以，是的，任何事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess the, yeah, a robot doing anything always gets me excited, even if it's something that hasn't been done before.
zh: 我想是的，是的，一个机器人做任何事总是让我兴奋，即使那是以前从未做过的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess one thing that we've been doing recently is having robots use knives to slice vegetables.
zh: 我想我们最近一直在做的一件事是让机器人使用刀来切蔬菜。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that there's a lot that you can do there once you actually can use knives safely, which is one thing that we've done recently.
zh: 我认为一旦你实际上能安全地使用刀，那里你可以做很多事情，那是我们最近做的一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, and then the last question is, how can someone break into robotics from a software engineering background?
zh: 好的，然后最后一个问题是，一个拥有软件工程背景的人如何进入机器人领域？

speaker: Unknown
en: Great.
zh: 很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that the, I guess first there's a lot of software engineering in robotics.
zh: 所以我认为，我想首先机器人领域有很多软件工程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's, I think you could try joining a robotics company as a software engineer.
zh: 所以有，我认为你可以尝试作为软件工程师加入一家机器人公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then another thing that I would mention, and I've actually seen someone take this path.
zh: 然后我会提到的另一件事，而且我实际上看到有人走过这条路。

speaker: Unknown
en: So someone who actually now works at Physical Intelligence, her name is Jenny, she...
zh: 所以实际上现在在 Physical Intelligence 工作的人，她的名字是 Jenny，她……

speaker: Unknown
en: I worked in trading algorithmic trading for a while then she worked at Harvey and was doing legal stuff and she was really excited about robots and so she bought a cheap robot and basically in her bedroom like played around with it and tried like fine-tuning an open source model and trying to get it to do something and then she shared what she had done and she sent me a cold email and was like hey can I like I'm interested in working in your lab and it seemed like her profile was promising and that she actually like
zh: 我在算法交易领域工作了一段时间，然后她在 Harvey 工作，做法律相关的事情，她对机器人真的很兴奋，所以她买了一个便宜的机器人，基本上在她的卧室里摆弄它，尝试微调开源模型并试图让它做点什么，然后她分享了她的所做所为，给我发了一封冷邮件，说嘿我可以我对在你的实验室工作感兴趣，而且她的 profile 看起来很有前景，而且她实际上喜欢

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually got out there and tried it and done it, and she was really excited about that.
zh: 我实际上出去了并尝试了并做到了，而且她对此真的很兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now she works at Physical Intelligence.
zh: 现她在 Physical Intelligence 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I think just getting your feet wet, trying stuff out, and learning from that experience, and then using that experience to share with people, have it on your resume, and so forth, I think is a great way to do stuff.
zh: 但是是的，我认为只是涉足其中，尝试东西，并从那个经验中学习，然后使用那个经验与人分享，把它放在你的简历上等等，我认为做事情的一个很好的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And fortunately, there's a lot of open source stuff out there that can allow you to get started on those kinds of things.
zh: 幸运的是，那里有很多开源的东西可以让你开始做这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great.
zh: 很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was the last question.
zh: 那是最后一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks, everyone, for listening.
zh: 谢谢，大家，收听。
